title: Capacity estimation
summary: Back-of-the-envelope numbers with stated assumptions: QPS, storage, bandwidth and cache size.

questions.prompt: 100 million active users each make 20 requests per day. What is the average number of requests per second? (A day has 86,400 seconds.)
Using the same 23,148 average requests per second, and an assumed peak factor of 3, what is the peak rate?
10 million new posts are created each day, about 1 KB each (1 KB = 1,000 bytes). How much new storage per day?
At 10 GB of new data per day, how much in a year of 365 days?
23,148 requests per second each return a 10 KB response (1 KB = 1,000 bytes). What outbound bandwidth is that?
You want to cache the 1 million hottest items, about 2 KB each (1 KB = 1,000 bytes). Roughly how much memory?
5 million videos are uploaded per day. How many uploads per second is that on average?
Why should an estimate state its peak factor instead of just quoting a peak number?
options: The factor is an assumption that changes the answer; stating it lets others check and adjust it
Peak numbers are always 3× the average
